findings.title: retryCount cleanup not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The new deleteMany adds an OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` that has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, while the sibling branch does. Today only this SMS handler ever increments `retryCount`, so only SMS rows are affected in practice — but the column is on the general `WorkflowReminder` model and the migration defaults all rows to 0. As soon as any other path (a future EMAIL/WHATSAPP scheduler, a backfill, an admin tool, manual SQL) sets `retryCount` on a non-SMS reminder, this query will silently delete those rows along with the SMS ones. The branch should be scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or the second OR arm should be merged into the first with `AND`) so the cleanup cannot reach reminders of other methods.

findings.title: Find-then-update is not atomic; concurrent cron ticks can double-schedule and double-count retries
findings.body: The handler does `findMany({ scheduled: false })` and then, in a separate loop, calls `twilio.scheduleSMS` and finally updates `scheduled = true` (or `retryCount += 1`). There is no transaction, row lock, or `update ... where { scheduled: false } returning ...` guard, so if two cron invocations overlap (or the previous run is retried while still in flight) both will fetch the same `scheduled: false` row and both will call Twilio, producing two scheduled SMS messages for the same reminder. The new retryCount increment makes the failure path worse: if Twilio throws, both concurrent handlers hit the catch block and both write `retryCount: N + 1`, so retryCount can be undercounted (e.g. two simultaneous failures on a row at retryCount=0 both write 1 instead of 2) and the row may survive an extra round instead of being deleted. This should be made atomic, e.g. by doing an `updateMany` with `where: { id, scheduled: false }` returning the row, or by wrapping the scheduling call in a transaction with a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`.

findings.title: Permanent SMS drops after retry exhaustion are silent
findings.body: When a reminder crosses `retryCount > 1` it is deleted by the next cron tick with no log line and no notification. The catch path only logs the underlying `twilio.scheduleSMS` error; once the row is later deleted by the `retryCount > 1` branch there is no trace that the user was supposed to receive an SMS at all. Given this is precisely the case the PR is trying to surface ("after scheduling failed twice we delete"), the deleteMany should at minimum log the reminder id, booking uid, workflowStep, and last error so that the dropped reminders are visible in logs and can be alerted on or surfaced to the organizer.
